messages.author: 6a75f6f91a59c568
messages.subject: fixing parameter in simsem
parts:
Hi, all.

I encountered too much improper solution when fixing parameters in the 'simsem' context.
Can I solve too much improper solution issue?

Seongho
  
  # Specifying population (true-parameter) model
    pop.model <- "
    F1 =~ .70*y1 + .75*y2 + .80*y3 + .85*y4 + .65*y5
    F2 =~ .70*y5 + .75*y6 + .80*y7 + .85*y8 + .65*y9
    F3 =~ .70*y9 + .75*y10 + .80*y11 + .85*y12 + .65*y13
    F4 =~ .70*y13 + .75*y14 + .80*y15 + .85*y16

    F1 ~~ .30*F3
    F2 ~~ .35*F3
    F2 ~~ .40*F4

    F1 ~~ 0*F2
    F1 ~~ 0*F4
    F3 ~~ 0*F4

    F1 ~~ 1*F1
    F2 ~~ 1*F2
    F3 ~~ 1*F3
    F4 ~~ 1*F4

    y1 ~~ .51*y1
    y2 ~~ .4375*y2
    y3 ~~ .36*y3
    y4 ~~ .2775*y4
    y5 ~~ .0875*y5
    y6 ~~ .4375*y6
    y7 ~~ .36*y7
    y8 ~~ .2775*y8
    y9 ~~ .0875*y9
    y10 ~~ .4375*y10
    y11 ~~ .36*y11
    y12 ~~ .2775*y12
    y13 ~~ .0875*y13
    y14 ~~ .4375*y14
    y15 ~~ .36*y15
    y16 ~~ .2775*y16
    y2 ~~ .14*y10
    y7 ~~ .15*y11
    y8 ~~ .16*y16
    "

  # ... and set simulation model for the true-parameter condition (checkup data generation bias)
    c0.model <-"
    F1 =~ NA*y1 + NA*y2 + NA*y3 + NA*y4 + NA*y5
    F2 =~ NA*y5 + NA*y6 + NA*y7 + NA*y8 + NA*y9
    F3 =~ NA*y9 + NA*y10 + NA*y11 + NA*y12 + NA*y13
    F4 =~ NA*y13 + NA*y14 + NA*y15 + NA*y16

    F1 ~~ Z1*F1
    F2 ~~ Z2*F2
    F3 ~~ Z3*F3
    F4 ~~ Z4*F4

    F1 ~~ 0*F2
    F1 ~~ NA*F3 # NA means forcely set to 'free parameter'
    F1 ~~ 0*F4
    F2 ~~ NA*F3
    F2 ~~ NA*F4
    F3 ~~ 0*F4

    y2 ~~ y10
    y7 ~~ y11
    y8 ~~ y16

    # Constrain parameters
    Z1 == 1
    Z2 == 1
    Z3 == 1
    Z4 == 1
    "

  # output of c0 (population model itself)
    c0.output_50 <- sim(nRep = 500, model = c0.model, n = 50, generate = pop.model, lavaanfun = "cfa", multicore = F, seed = 20161020, completeRep = T)

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: fixing parameter in simsem
parts: I think the issue is occuring with how you're setting the scale of your latent variables. It looks like you're fixing each latent variance to 1 using the labels Z1-Z4. If you simply set the variances to 1 in the code (eliminating the labels z1-z4 ) things should work a little better. So this:

F1 ~~ Z1*F1
    F2 ~~ Z2*F2
    F3 ~~ Z3*F3
    F4 ~~ Z4*F4
Should be this:

F1 ~~ 1*F1
    F2 ~~ 1*F2
    F3 ~~ 1*F3
    F4 ~~ 1*F4

And then you can remove the Constrain parameters section.

I should also note that with an N of 50 you're likely to run into some improper solutions even if your model is correct.

I think the issue is occuring with how you're setting the scale of your latent variables. It looks like you're fixing each latent variance to 1 using the labels Z1-Z4. If you simply set the variances to 1 in the code (eliminating the labels z1-z4 ) things should work a little better. So this:

    F1 ~~ Z1*F1
    F2 ~~ Z2*F2
    F3 ~~ Z3*F3
    F4 ~~ Z4*F4

Should be this:

    F1 ~~ 1*F1
    F2 ~~ 1*F2
    F3 ~~ 1*F3
    F4 ~~ 1*F4

And then you can remove the Constrain parameters section.

I should also note that with an N of 50 you're likely to run into some improper solutions even if your model is correct.
